reported.title: Fill valve drops out on noisy level readings (no input filtering)
reported.description: readLevelCm() (lines 28-33) takes a single raw analogRead with no averaging or hysteresis, and the state machine at lines 73-80 acts on that one sample each 40 ms tick. A brief noise spike above 25.0 cm moves the state to ST_RUN (line 77-79), and driveOutputs() (line 37) then drives D9 LOW; the measured evidence shows D9 not HIGH for 870 ms while required during the glitch-spike scenario, and 5380 ms in the spike-to-25cm scenario. D9 was in the wrong state for 3850 ms across 5 interval(s), first at 1.63 s: D9 was not HIGH for 870 ms while required (grace 600 ms).

reported.title: Motor runs with insufficient water; no RUN->IDLE exit path
reported.description: The state machine has no transition from ST_RUN back to ST_IDLE when level falls below RUN_MIN_CM; lines 73-80 only handle IDLE->FILL and FILL->RUN, so once in ST_RUN the motor stays HIGH via line 38 regardless of level. Measured evidence shows D10 not LOW for 340 ms at 7.66 s in the nominal ramp and not LOW for 870 ms during glitch spikes, and the premature spike-to-RUN leaves the motor on with low water. D10 was in the wrong state for 3850 ms across 5 interval(s), first at 1.63 s: D10 was not LOW for 870 ms while required (grace 600 ms).

truth.description: RUN state never exits when level drops

truth_for_judge.description: RUN state never exits when level drops

exposing_checks.behaviour: D10 must follow its stimulus; LOW when A0 < 20; within 600 ms (Motor off below 20 cm)

judge_input.spec:
- Level probe on A0 at 10 mV/cm; fill valve on D9; drum motor on D10; reset on D4 (pull-up).
- States: IDLE (both outputs OFF), FILL (valve D9 HIGH until level >= 25.0 cm), RUN (motor D10 HIGH while level stays >= 20.0 cm), then IDLE.
- Leave RUN and return to IDLE when level drops below 20.0 cm; motor D10 must go LOW within 600 ms.
- Enter FILL from IDLE when level is below 10.0 cm.
- Holding D4 LOW forces IDLE immediately.
- Print `laundry st=<0|1|2> cm=<n>` every 1000 ms.
